editorial:
If you grew up loving Adam Sandler's goofy comedies, this one feels like a warm Halloween hug. Hubie Dubois is the town punching bag in Salem, Massachusetts, but he takes his job as the neighborhood safety monitor way too seriously. When strange things start happening on Halloween night, nobody believes him at first. The movie leans hard into silly costumes, slapstick jokes, and a surprisingly sweet heart. It is not trying to be scary or deep. It just wants you to laugh and feel good.

Sandler plays Hubie with a goofy voice and big heart, and the cast is packed with familiar faces who clearly had fun making it. The pacing is quick, the jokes come fast, and there are plenty of silly sight gags. The downside is that some jokes repeat and the story is pretty predictable. Still, if you want a light, family-friendly Halloween movie night, this is a solid pick. It is best enjoyed with snacks and zero expectations.
endingExplained: In the final act, Hubie discovers the real threat is a group of escaped mental patients and a vengeful neighbor. After a chaotic chase through Salem, Hubie saves the town and finally earns respect from everyone who mocked him. The twist reveals his mom was behind some of the pranks to protect him. In the end, Hubie gets the girl, the town throws him a parade, and Halloween is saved.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Adam Sandler comedies and lighthearted Halloween fun.
